blocks.raw: # Customise Member Care UI using Extension
blocks.text: Customise Member Care UI using Extension

blocks.raw: # Introduction
blocks.text: Introduction

blocks.raw: You can customize the Member Care user interface (UI) to meet your organization’s specific needs using the [Vulcan](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/vulcan#/) application extension. This feature enables you to integrate and extend Member Care with additional functionality to support your operations. The applications that you are adding appear under a specific tab on the Membercare UI.

blocks.raw: ## Key benefits
blocks.text: Key benefits

blocks.raw: Using the Vulcan application extension in Member Care provides several advantages:
blocks.text: Using the Vulcan application extension in Member Care provides several advantages:

blocks.raw: * ### Non-override functionality
blocks.text: Non-override functionality

blocks.raw: The existing Member Care features remain intact. Vulcan integrates with them without overriding the default behavior or configurations.
blocks.text: The existing Member Care features remain intact. Vulcan integrates with them without overriding the default behavior or configurations.

blocks.raw: * ### Utilization of existing containers
blocks.text: Utilization of existing containers

blocks.raw: Vulcan supports customization using predefined containers in Member Care. A container is a designated UI section that groups and displays related information or components, helping maintain a structured and consistent layout.
blocks.text: Vulcan supports customization using predefined containers in Member Care. A container is a designated UI section that groups and displays related information or components, helping maintain a structured and consistent layout.

blocks.raw: * ### Multiple extension variants
blocks.text: Multiple extension variants

blocks.raw:
You can choose between different versions of a MemberCare Extension, such as UAT and Prod, from the dropdown.
The UAT (Unit Acceptance Testing)  version includes the latest updates that may still be under testing, while the Production version (prod) is the stable, production-ready build.
For production organizations, it’s recommended to select the Prod version when configuring the extension.

blocks.raw: ## Application availability
blocks.text: Application availability

blocks.raw: The availability of applications depends on your organization’s configuration:
blocks.text: The availability of applications depends on your organization’s configuration:

blocks.raw:
* Sharingan-enabled organizations: You can choose either Sharingan or Vulcan applications.
* Vulcan-only organizations: You can choose only Vulcan applications.
* New organizations: You can choose only Vulcan applications.

blocks.raw: ## Adding a Vulcan extension in Member Care
blocks.text: Adding a Vulcan extension in Member Care

blocks.raw: Follow these steps to add an extension to the Member Care UI:
blocks.text: Follow these steps to add an extension to the Member Care UI:

blocks.raw:
1. Open Member Care for the organization where you want to add the Vulcan extension.

2. Click the **Settings** (gear icon).
   The Member Care Extensions page opens, listing all extensions for your organization.

3. Click **Add Extension**.
   A new row appears to define the extension details.

   <Image align="center" border={true} src="https://files.readme.io/8b05630a36d590cb5b4a8d0b8b222b9f76c7b0dc65456b3f922ddafaaf8b0f91-Add_extension.png" className="border" />

4. Under **Extension Name**, enter a unique name for the new extension.
   This name will appear in the Member Care UI.

5. Under **Map Extensions to External Apps**, click the **Select App** dropdown.
   The available extensions Vulcan, Sharingan, or both appear.

6. Expand the extension you want to use and select it under the appropriate environment. Some extensions may have both User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and Production versions, while others may have only one.
   **Tip:** Choose the **Prod** version if available.

   <Image align="center" border={true} src="https://files.readme.io/2244d835ab4d1eaa89783ce469c527dc9a15eb658a5653b9f03190e18a168692-GIF3_6.gif" className="border" />

7. Under **Containers**, click the **Select Container** drop-down list, and choose where you want the extension to appear in the Member Care UI.
   **Note**: Currently, only the **Member Profile/tab** is available.

   <Image align="center" border={true} src="https://files.readme.io/9264c71d3f82d2744e5f90efb8ca12a62d250984991dce93a832c0517b065130-Select-container.png" className="border" />

8. Click **✓ (Save)**.

blocks.raw: ## Edit a Vulcan extension in Member Care
blocks.text: Edit a Vulcan extension in Member Care

blocks.raw: To edit an existing Vulcan extension in the Member Care user interface:
blocks.text: To edit an existing Vulcan extension in the Member Care user interface:

blocks.raw:
1. Open Member Care for the organization where you want to edit the Vulcan extension. 2. Click the **Settings** (gear icon). The **Member Care Extensions** page opens, displaying all extensions currently in use for your organization. 3. Hover over the **More options (...)** icon next to the extension you want to edit, and select **Edit**. You can now update the following fields: * Map extensions to external apps * Containers
4. To edit **Map extensions to external apps**, click the dropdown under **Map extensions to external apps**. Then, expand the required extension and select it under the appropriate environment. Some extensions may have both UAT and Production versions, while others may have only one. **Tip**: Choose the Production version if available. 5. To edit **Containers**, click the dropdown under **Container** and choose the location where you want the extension to appear in the Member Care UI. **Note**: Currently, only the **Member Profile/Tab** is available. 6. Click **✓ (Save)** to apply your changes.

blocks.raw: ## Delete a Vulcan extension in Member Care
blocks.text: Delete a Vulcan extension in Member Care

blocks.raw: Follow these steps to delete a Vulcan extension from the Member Care UI:
blocks.text: Follow these steps to delete a Vulcan extension from the Member Care UI:

blocks.raw:
1. Open Member Care for the organization where you want to delete the Vulcan extension.

2. Click the **Settings (gear icon).**
   The Member Care Extensions page opens, displaying all extensions currently in use for your organization.

3. Hover over the **More options (...)** icon next to the extension you want to delete, and select **Delete**.

4. A confirmation message appears. Click **Yes,Sure** to confirm.

   <Image align="center" border={true} src="https://files.readme.io/95593a89f31995dedcc57b9f4af9b9ae48a2a4a3c8e72019438f3b516309805c-Delete.png" className="border" />

blocks.raw: # FAQs
blocks.text: FAQs

blocks.raw: 1. What is the Vulcan application extension in Member Care?
blocks.text: What is the Vulcan application extension in Member Care?

blocks.raw: Answer: The Vulcan application extension allows you to customize the Member Care UI to match your organization’s specific needs.
blocks.text: Answer: The Vulcan application extension allows you to customize the Member Care UI to match your organization’s specific needs.

blocks.raw: 2. Who can use the Vulcan application?
blocks.text: Who can use the Vulcan application?

blocks.raw: Answer: Application availability depends on your organization’s configuration:
blocks.text: Answer: Application availability depends on your organization’s configuration:

blocks.raw:
* Sharingan-enabled organizations: Can use both Sharingan and Vulcan applications.
* Vulcan-only organizations: Can use only Vulcan applications.
* New organizations: Can use only Vulcan applications.
blocks.text: Sharingan-enabled organizations: Can use both Sharingan and Vulcan applications.Vulcan-only organizations: Can use only Vulcan applications.New organizations: Can use only Vulcan applications.

blocks.raw: 3. What are containers in Member Care?
blocks.text: What are containers in Member Care?

blocks.raw: Answer: A container is a predefined UI section in Member Care that organizes and displays related information or components. Containers define where your Vulcan extension appears—for example, in the Member Profile section or Tab section.
blocks.text: Answer: A container is a predefined UI section in Member Care that organizes and displays related information or components. Containers define where your Vulcan extension appears—for example, in the Member Profile section or Tab section.

blocks.text: What is the scope of customization supported through Vulcan?

blocks.raw: **Note**: Adding widgets, embedding content directly on existing pages, or customizing “More Actions” is not supported.

blocks.raw: 6. Can I test an app before going live?
blocks.text: Can I test an app before going live?

blocks.raw: Answer: Yes, you can. You can test integrations in the User Acceptance Testing (UAT) environment before deploying to production. Both environments are supported in MemberCare.

Any user with Member Care access can add, modify, or delete Vulcan extensions.

blocks.raw: 9. Are there any current limitations?
blocks.text: Are there any current limitations?

blocks.raw: Answer: Yes. The following actions are not supported at this time:
blocks.text: Answer: Yes. The following actions are not supported at this time:

blocks.raw:
* Adding extensions under More Actions.
* Adding extensions as widgets.
* Embedding content directly within existing Member Care pages.

10. What should I do if my Vulcan extension does not appear in Member Care?
    Answer:
blocks.text:
What should I do if my Vulcan extension does not appear in Member Care?
Answer:

blocks.raw:
* Verify that the extension is saved and mapped to the correct environment (UAT or Production).
* Check that the selected container exists in Member Care.
* Ensure your app is deployed and active.
  If the issue persists, contact the PSV team for support.
